newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CAR SALES RISE 36 PERCENT IN EIGHT MONTHS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CAR SALES RISE 36 PERCENT IN EIGHT MONTHS.

text.p: New car sales in Poland jumped nearly 36 percent in the first eight months of 1996 compared with the same period last year, PAP news agency said on Thursday.

PAP quoted a report by the Samar agency, which monitors the domestic car market, as saying that 259,665 units were sold over the period. In the first seven months of this year new car sales reached 230,766.
The Polish unit of Fiat Spa led the market with 109,437 cars and its market share was 42 percent.
Other top sellers include Daewoo-FSO, a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Corp, General Motors' German unit Adam Opel AG and France's Renault.
Samar Director Wojciech Drzewiecki earlier predicted that Poland's auto sales should exceed 300,000 this year, compared to about 265,000 in 1995.
The increase is fuelled by growth in real wages and more attractive terms of bank financing of car purchases.
